subject: Agriculture
title: China's South-North Water Transfer
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: China's South-North Water Transfer.

hook.text: Southern China has abundant water. Northern China—where the wheat grows—is running dry.

buildup.text: China is building canals to transfer 45 billion cubic meters of water per year from south to north.

discovery.text: Three routes span thousands of kilometers. The eastern route follows the ancient Grand Canal alignment.

twist.text: The project costs over $80 billion and displaces hundreds of thousands of people from reservoir areas.

climax.text: Critics say conservation and efficiency could solve the problem without moving a single drop.

punchline.text: Move mountains or save water? China chose to move the rivers.

quiz.question: How much water will China's South-North Transfer project move annually?
